subject: Engineering Mechanics
summary: impulse–momentum (linear and angular), energy methods, collisions and virtual work
next_day: Strength of Materials, Stress, Strain & Mohr's Circle

questions.text: A 20 g bullet moving horizontally at 400 m/s embeds itself in a 2 kg block resting on a smooth horizontal floor. The common velocity just after impact (in m/s) is ______
solution: Concept: During the very short impact, external horizontal impulse is zero, so linear momentum is conserved (energy is not).
KE before = ½(0.02)(400²) = 1600 J; KE after = ½(2.02)(3.96²) = 15.8 J → about 99 % is lost as heat and deformation.
Exam tip: In a plastic impact with a heavy target, the fraction of KE lost is M/(m + M), nearly all of it.

questions.text: A 10 g bullet is fired into a 1.99 kg wooden block hanging from light strings (ballistic pendulum) and stays inside it. The block rises by 0.2 m, as shown. The speed of the bullet was (g = 9.81 m/s²)
solution: Concept: Two stages. Impact: momentum conserved. Swing: mechanical energy conserved.
Swing: V = √(2gh) = √(2 × 9.81 × 0.2) = 1.981 m/s (block + bullet just after impact)
Exam tip: Never apply energy conservation across the impact itself; KE is lost when the bullet embeds.

questions.text: A ball dropped from a height of 4 m on to a hard floor rebounds to a height of 2.25 m. The coefficient of restitution between the ball and the floor is ______
solution: Concept: e = (speed of separation)/(speed of approach). For a fixed floor e = v/u.
Exam tip: e = √(h2/h1), not h2/h1 (0.5625 is the trap).

questions.text: A 2 kg sphere moving at 6 m/s makes a direct central impact with a 4 kg sphere at rest. If e = 0.5, the velocities of the 2 kg and 4 kg spheres after impact are
solution: Concept: Use momentum conservation and Newton's law of restitution together.
Momentum: 2(6) = 2v<sub>1</sub> + 4v<sub>2</sub> → v<sub>1</sub> + 2v<sub>2</sub> = 6
Restitution: v<sub>2</sub> − v<sub>1</sub> = 0.5 × 6 = 3
Solving: 3v2 = 9 → v2 = 3 m/s, v1 = 0 m/s (the 2 kg sphere stops).
Check: 2 m/s and 2 m/s is the perfectly plastic case (e = 0); −2 and 4 is the elastic case (e = 1).
Exam tip: Write restitution as (v2 − v1) = e(u1 − u2) with one sign convention throughout.

questions.text: A 0.2 kg ball at rest is struck by a force that varies with time as shown (a triangle, peak 500 N at 0.02 s, back to zero at 0.04 s). The speed of the ball just after the blow (in m/s) is ______
solution: Concept: Impulse = area under the F–t curve = change of momentum.
Average force = 10/0.04 = 250 N, half the peak, as expected for a triangle.
Exam tip: When a graph is given, impulse is always an area. Do not multiply the peak force by the whole time (that gives 100 m/s).

questions.text: A 2 kg block sliding at 3 m/s on a smooth floor hits a light spring of stiffness 2000 N/m. The maximum compression of the spring is
solution: Concept: Smooth floor → all the KE of the block is stored as spring energy at maximum compression.
½mv² = ½kx² → x = v√(m/k)
Exam tip: At maximum compression the block is momentarily at rest. With friction, subtract μmg·x from the left side.

questions.text: A 5 kg block starts from rest and slides 4 m down a rough plane inclined at 30° (μ = 0.2). Its speed at the end of the 4 m (in m/s) is ______
solution: Concept: Work–energy theorem: net work done by all forces = change in KE.
Work by gravity = mg sin 30° × 4 = 5 × 9.81 × 0.5 × 4 = 98.1 J
Exam tip: The mass cancels: v = √(2gL(sin θ − μ cos θ)). Useful for a quick check.

questions.text: A disc (I = 0.5 kg·m²) spins freely at 10 rad/s on a frictionless vertical shaft. A second disc (I = 0.3 kg·m²), initially at rest, is dropped onto it and they rotate together. The final angular speed is
solution: Concept: No external torque about the shaft → angular momentum is conserved.
KE falls from 25 J to 15.62 J: 37.5 % is lost in the friction between the discs.
Exam tip: This is the rotational version of a plastic collision. Angular momentum is kept, KE is not.

questions.text: A car of mass 1000 kg climbs a slope of 1 in 20 (along the slope) at a steady 36 km/h. The road and air resistance total 500 N. The power developed by the engine (in kW) is ______
solution: Concept: At steady speed, tractive force = resistance + component of weight along the slope. Power = force × speed.
Weight component = mg sin θ = 1000 × 9.81 × (1/20) = 490.5 N
Tractive force = 490.5 + 500 = 990.5 N; v = 36 km/h = 10 m/s
Exam tip: '1 in 20' means sin θ = 1/20 (along the slope) unless the question says otherwise.

questions.text: Two equal light links AB and BC are pinned together at B. A is a pin and C is a roller on the same level, as shown. A vertical load P = 100 N acts at B. Using the principle of virtual work, the horizontal force Q at C needed for equilibrium when θ = 60° is
solution: Concept: Give the mechanism a virtual displacement δθ. Reactions at A and C do no work, so only P and Q appear.
Coordinates: y<sub>B</sub> = L sin θ, x<sub>C</sub> = 2L cos θ → δy<sub>B</sub> = L cos θ δθ, δx<sub>C</sub> = −2L sin θ δθ
δW = −P δy<sub>B</sub> − Q δx<sub>C</sub> = (−PL cos θ + 2QL sin θ) δθ = 0
Exam tip: Virtual work skips the reactions entirely. Choose coordinates from a fixed point (A) so the signs come out naturally.

questions.text: A ball strikes a smooth horizontal floor at 10 m/s, its path making 30° with the floor. If e = 0.6, the speed of the ball just after the bounce (in m/s) is ______
solution: Concept: Smooth floor: the component along the floor is unchanged. Restitution acts only on the normal component.
Along the floor: 10 cos 30° = 8.66 m/s (unchanged)
Normal: 10 sin 30° = 5 m/s → after bounce 0.6 × 5 = 3 m/s
Exam tip: On a smooth surface the ball always leaves at a flatter angle than it arrived (when e < 1).

questions.text: A uniform rod of mass 3 kg and length 1 m lies at rest on a smooth horizontal table. A horizontal impulse of 6 N·s is applied at one end, perpendicular to the rod. The angular velocity of the rod just after the blow is
solution: Concept: Linear impulse = change of linear momentum; moment of the impulse about G = change of angular momentum about G.
Linear: 6 = 3 v<sub>G</sub> → v<sub>G</sub> = 2 m/s
The far end moves at v<sub>G</sub> − ω(0.5) = 2 − 6 = −4 m/s, i.e. opposite to the blow.
Exam tip: The point 2/3 of the length from the struck end is momentarily at rest (vG − ω d = 0 → d = 1/6 m beyond G).

questions.text: A 2 kg block is dropped from rest 0.5 m above the top of a vertical spring of stiffness 4000 N/m, as shown. The maximum compression of the spring (in mm) is ______
solution: Concept: Energy conservation from release to maximum compression. Gravity does work over the whole drop h + x, not just h.
Exam tip: Ignoring the extra drop x gives √(2mgh/k) = 70.0 mm, a typical wrong option.

questions.text: A smooth sphere moving on a smooth table strikes an identical sphere at rest in a glancing (oblique) perfectly elastic collision. After impact the two spheres move
opts: in directions at 90° to each other
in directions at 45° to each other
questions.ans: (B) in directions at 90° to each other
solution: Concept: Equal masses, elastic: momentum gives u⃗ = v⃗1 + v⃗2; energy gives u² = v1² + v2².
Squaring the momentum equation: u² = v<sub>1</sub>² + v<sub>2</sub>² + 2 v⃗<sub>1</sub>·v⃗<sub>2</sub>
Comparing: v⃗1·v⃗2 = 0 → the velocities are perpendicular (unless the impact is head-on, when the first sphere simply stops).
Exam tip: This is why a snooker cue ball and object ball fly off at right angles after a thin cut.

questions.text: A 20 kg block rests on a horizontal floor (μ<sub>s</sub> = μ<sub>k</sub> = 0.2). A horizontal force P = 10t newtons (t in s) is applied from t = 0. The speed of the block at t = 8 s (in m/s) is ______
solution: Concept: The block does not move until P exceeds limiting friction. Apply impulse–momentum only from that instant.
Limiting friction = 0.2 × 20 × 9.81 = 39.24 N → motion starts at 10t0 = 39.24, t0 = 3.924 s
Impulse of P from t<sub>0</sub> to 8 s = ∫10t dt = 5(8² − 3.924²) = 243.01 N·s
Impulse of friction = 39.24 × (8 − 3.924) = 159.94 N·s
Exam tip: Integrating from t = 0 with kinetic friction acting throughout gives only 0.30 m/s, the classic mistake. Before t0 static friction exactly cancels P.
